text:
maria: Quick q — when creating an experiment in Console, should variant weights be decoupled from route-level traffic caps? e.g. weights sum to 100 but route cap is 10% (soft staging) :thinking_face:

sam: yes. treat route cap as allocation then distribute by weights inside that allocation. users expect weights to be logical, not absolute traffic.

kevin: agree. also need to show an "effective traffic" preview in the UI: weight -> effective % of total users. otherwise operators get surprised. :eyes:

anya: UX thing: show a tiny preview bar next to each variant with both "weight" and "est. traffic". put a tooltip that explains route cap. simple copy: "Route cap limits experiment exposure; weights split the allocated traffic."

maria: technical question: on the API side, do we validate weight sum == 100 or allow partial sums and normalize? current backend normalizes but console shows error if !=100. inconsistent.

sam: backend normalizes because variants are logical buckets. console should mirror that behavior and let user save a partial config (with a clear normalized preview). error is annoying.

kevin: +1 for normalization but add a guard: if normalization would change any variant by >20% show a confirmation modal. that prevents accidental massive shifts.

anya: another guard: per-variant QPS caps. ops asked for per-variant ceiling to prevent noisy variants from hogging capacity. we should let users set `qps_cap` per variant or fall back to route-level cap.

maria: makes sense. how do we expose that in the API? current experiment API only accepts `variants: [{id, weight, metadata}]`. we could add `qps_cap` optional field. backwards compatible.

sam: small API debate: should we call it `qps_cap` or `throttle_rps`? `qps` is familiar to infra but `rps` is more generic. I'm leaning `rps_cap` for clarity.

kevin: prefer `rps_cap`. also include units in docs and UI (rps).

anya: telemetry hooks: we need deterministic event naming for rollout metrics. propose `experiment.assign` (when assignment happens), `experiment.eval` (model/prompt evaluation step), `experiment.win` (conversion). include `experiment_id`, `variant_id`, `seed`, `assignment_key` in payload.

maria: minor nit: we currently use `user_id` in other telemetry. `assignment_key` was introduced for anonymous bucketing (cookie, device). mixing both will fragment signals. Recommend `assignment_key` as canonical field and alias `user_id` if present.

sam: +1 on canonical `assignment_key`. also include `assignment_method` (e.g., "user_id", "cookie", "cookie+seed") so downstream can filter.

kevin: oh and add `effective_weight` to telemetry so we can correlate expected vs actual traffic by variant. helps detect normalization surprises.

rollouts-bot: (automated) note: remember to update Console docs and API changelog when `rps_cap` lands.

maria: final asks for the Console PR: 1) change save behavior to normalize weights and show preview; 2) add optional `rps_cap` field in variant edit; 3) add preview bar + confirmation modal for >20% normalization delta; 4) wire telemetry fields `assignment_key`, `assignment_method`, `effective_weight`.

sam: i'll pick up the backend changes (API and normalization) this week. kevin/anya can you do the Console bits? i'll add telemetry schema to the infra repo.

anya: can do, i'll open a design+implementation issue and drop a quick mock later today. :thumbsup:

kevin: will add the preview bar prototype and accessibility notes.

maria: awesome. leaving this thread as the spec. if anyone wants to add edge cases (multi-target experiments, shard routing), drop them here.

sam: thanks all — filing follow-ups.

rollouts-bot: (automated) ticket created: EXPERIMENTS-4123 — "Normalize-weight-save + per-variant rps cap + telemetry" by sam.
